parts.text: Most expert work we see is like this. Musical recordings don’t include the bad takes and jam sessions, published books leave out the

drafts, and scientific papers don’t mention the years of false starts and dead ends.

In other words, what we actually see is a trace of the real process that produced it. These traces are what artificial intelligence (AI) models are

on – and as a result, they produce traces themselves, which are shaped like the products of thought but aren’t necessarily made the same way.

In a new paper, we argue that focusing on traces while leaving out process

current AI systems – and the same problem can arise for the people who use those systems.

Traces and friction

Newer “reasoning” models may print out a report of their steps, but that reported reasoning is itself another trace. It often fails to line up with the

computation driving the answer.

Agentic systems come slightly closer to real thinking. Here, a software “harness” around a large language model runs a loop, feeds results back, and introduces some genuine

revision into the process. But the chain of thought in the middle – the part produced by the large language model – is still a trace.

The gap is widest in creative domains. Painters and musicians sometimes talk about how their work was

by accidents and friction that happened while making it, such as paint running unexpectedly, or an instrument sounding “off”. AI models never encounter anything like this.

Use it or lose it

The human form of this problem is much older than AI. In 1997, an American Airlines

warned that pilots were becoming “children of the magenta line”.

They followed the plane’s flight computer so faithfully that their manual flying skills were

. Aviation has taken steps to manage automation dependency ever since.

The same thing happened when some medical clinics adopted AI-assisted colonoscopy, using software to flag possible polyps on the live camera feed. After a while, the skills of the human

began to erode: they detected fewer polyps when working without the AI system than they had before its introduction.

This effect has been seen in classrooms, too. High school mathematics students given unrestricted
AI support outperformed their peers when the tool was available, but scored lower once it was taken away.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Chemical evidence in ancient rocks helps scientists date the beginnings of plate tectonics.
A new CERN experiment could deepen understanding of the electron and fundamental physics.
Aboriginal astronomical knowledge explains celestial movements and their connections to life on Earth.
Learning from finished expressions of thought is different from learning the process of thinking.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: In education, and in any skilled enterprise, we need to consider how AI systems are designed and used to preserve more of the thinking and learning process.

questions.prompt: How does the article characterise the visible product of thinking?
options: As something entirely unrelated to any process
As a trace of the process that produced it
As proof that thinking never involves hidden steps
As a complete recording of every mental operation
